blocks.text: TWO KINGDOMS
Shemaiah the Nehelamite. Wrote from Babylon to the priests at Jerusalem asking why Jeremiah had not been reproved.
SCRIPTURE SAYS
“I sent him not” (Jeremiah 29:31)
ERA
Two kingdoms 930–586 BC
IN THE DAYS OF
Zedekiah
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW HE SPOKE
He “sent letters in thy name unto all the people that are at Jerusalem, and to Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests”.
THE CALL
How he spoke

He “sent letters in thy name unto all the people that are at Jerusalem, and to Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests”. The LORD's word says he “hath prophesied unto you”. Jeremiah 29:25 Jeremiah 29:31

From the textWhere the Hebrew and the King James Version have “Shemaiah the Nehelamite”, the Greek Septuagint has “Samæas the Ælamite” (Greek chapter 36:24, in Brenton's translation of 1844). Jeremiah 29:24 [1]
BEFORE THE KINGS
Before Zedekiah, king of Judah
KING OF JUDAH
Zedekiah, king of Judah
THE WORD GIVEN
What he prophesied
His letter against Jeremiah
“Now therefore why hast thou not reproved Jeremiah of Anathoth, which maketh himself a prophet to you?”
Jeremiah 29:27 (KJV) →
“This captivity is long: build ye houses, and dwell in them”
Jeremiah 29:28 (KJV) →
THE WORD TO …
To whom the word was spoken
TO ALL THE CAPTIVITY, CONCERNING SHEMAIAH
“Because that Shemaiah hath prophesied unto you, and I sent him not, and he caused you to trust in a lie”
Jeremiah 29:31 (KJV) →
Babylon · He wrote as one of the captives (“he sent unto us in Babylon”)
THE ANSWER GIVEN
The answer, and what came of it
THE WORD
SCRIPTURE REPORTS
COMPANIONS AND OPPONENTS
Who stood with him, and against him
Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest
Jeremiah
HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
Foretold: no man of his would dwell among the people, nor would he see the good to come. Jeremiah 29:32
TRADITION SAYS
No tradition is recorded here.
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 1
Jeremiah 29
PASSAGES · 1
Jeremiah 29:24–32
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
The text does not explain “Nehelamite”, and no place or family of that name appears elsewhere in Scripture.
Scripture does not say what Zephaniah did after reading the letter to Jeremiah, beyond reading it.
He is a different man from Shemaiah the man of God in Rehoboam's day (1 Kgs 12:22) and Shemaiah in Nehemiah 6:10.
